metadata.research_goal: Create backend-ready cycling records for injury risk, strength and conditioning, bike-fit triage, return-to-ride logic, pain rules, crash-risk controls, and load monitoring across recreational, road, gravel, MTB, indoor, triathlon, and racing cyclists.

key_concepts.name: Equipment-mediated repetitive load
key_concepts.summary: Cycling injury risk is shaped by training load and by how the rider contacts the bike: saddle, pedals/cleats, handlebars, reach, bar drop, crank/cadence choices, and surface.
key_concepts.backend_use: Do not prescribe ride volume or intensity without also checking fit changes, contact-point symptoms, and terrain or indoor exposure.

key_concepts.name: Cycling overuse hotspots
key_concepts.summary: Common non-traumatic complaint areas include knee, low back, neck/shoulder, hands/wrists, saddle/perineum, and Achilles/calf.
key_concepts.backend_use: Screen these areas during onboarding, after block changes, after bike-fit changes, and after long indoor or climbing blocks.

key_concepts.name: Low-back pain is often a posture-tolerance problem
key_concepts.summary: Cyclists sustain trunk flexion and hip flexion for long periods; symptoms often worsen when ride duration, aero posture, bar drop, or fatigue exceeds spinal and hip support capacity.
key_concepts.backend_use: Pair bike-position triage with trunk endurance, hip mobility, posterior-chain strength, and gradual duration progression.

key_concepts.name: Knee pain requires load and fit triage
key_concepts.summary: Cycling knee symptoms can reflect a mismatch among saddle height, saddle setback, cleat position, cadence, gearing, hill volume, and recent intensity or volume changes.
key_concepts.backend_use: Knee-pain rules should reduce provoking exposure and trigger fit review instead of only adding generic knee exercises.

key_concepts.name: Hand numbness is a contact-pressure warning
key_concepts.summary: Median and ulnar nerve symptoms can be provoked by sustained handlebar pressure, wrist extension, vibration, reach, and poor weight distribution.
key_concepts.backend_use: Any numbness, tingling, weakness, or loss of grip control should trigger fit/contact-point review and ride modification.

key_concepts.name: Saddle symptoms are not just tolerance
key_concepts.summary: Perineal numbness, genital symptoms, saddle sores, or skin breakdown should not be normalized as normal cycling adaptation.
key_concepts.backend_use: Escalate persistent numbness, skin breakdown, urinary/genital symptoms, or recurring saddle sores to medical or bike-fit review.

key_concepts.name: Achilles and calf symptoms combine load, ankle demand, and foot-pedal setup
key_concepts.summary: Achilles/calf irritation can follow rapid increases in ride duration, intensity, climbing, sprinting, low-cadence torque, cleat changes, or excessive ankle motion.
key_concepts.backend_use: Track recent exposure changes and foot-pedal setup before progressing hill repeats, standing climbing, or sprint work.

key_concepts.name: Load monitoring needs external and internal channels
key_concepts.summary: Distance, duration, power, elevation, and interval counts describe external load; RPE, heart-rate response, sleep, mood, soreness, pain, and motivation describe internal response.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use both sides before increasing training stress or attributing underperformance to fitness.

key_concepts.name: Overtraining is more than being tired
key_concepts.summary: Expected fatigue should recover with planned rest; persistent performance decline, mood disturbance, high perceived effort, poor sleep, recurrent illness, or loss of motivation suggests nonfunctional overreaching or overtraining risk.
key_concepts.backend_use: Hold or regress training when fatigue and performance markers diverge from planned load for multiple sessions.

key_concepts.name: Strength work supports cycling load tolerance
key_concepts.summary: Useful S&C for cyclists targets lower-body force capacity, hip/trunk endurance, posterior-chain support, single-leg control, shoulder/upper-back posture, and tissue resilience.
key_concepts.backend_use: Prescribe progressive strength that respects key rides and avoids turning gym work into extra untracked high-intensity fatigue.

key_concepts.name: Pain response drives progression
key_concepts.summary: A ride can be acceptable when symptoms are low, stable, and settle quickly; symptoms that worsen during the ride or remain worse the next day mean the dose or setup is too aggressive.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use during-ride and 24-hour symptom response as plan gates for return-to-ride and overuse management.

key_concepts.name: Crash risk is part of load management
key_concepts.summary: Fast descents, traffic, group riding, fatigue, technical surfaces, poor weather, and equipment defects increase risk even when metabolic load is low.
key_concepts.backend_use: Include route, surface, visibility, handling readiness, and equipment checks in session readiness and progression logic.

technical_models.name: Cycling load channels
technical_models.backend_use: Store cycling load as multiple exposure channels because the same weekly hours can create very different tissue and safety risks.

technical_models.name: Knee pain fit and exposure map
technical_models.backend_use: When knee symptoms appear, reduce intensity and low-cadence torque while prompting fit and cleat review before adding more knee-loading work.

technical_models.name: Low-back tolerance triangle
technical_models.backend_use: Low-back symptoms should trigger review of posture exposure and off-bike support capacity, not only stretching.

technical_models.name: Contact-point symptom map
technical_models.backend_use: Symptoms at contact points should be interpreted as signals about pressure distribution, reach, bar height, saddle choice, shoe/cleat setup, and tissue tolerance.

technical_models.name: Bike-fit change risk window
technical_models.rule: Treat saddle, cleat, crank, handlebar, shoe, pedal, or aero-position changes as new loading stimuli for at least two weeks.
technical_models.backend_use: Avoid pairing major fit changes with high-volume, high-intensity, long climbing, or race weeks.

technical_models.name: Pain monitoring gate
rules: Green: no pain or mild symptoms that do not increase during the ride and return to baseline by the next morning.
Yellow: symptoms increase during the ride, alter movement, or remain elevated the next day; reduce dose and review setup.
Red: sharp pain, neurological symptoms, swelling, traumatic injury, saddle numbness that persists, or symptoms that worsen across sessions; stop and seek qualified review.
technical_models.backend_use: Use as return-to-ride and plan-adjustment logic for overuse complaints.

technical_models.name: Strength integration model
phases: foundation: technique, trunk, hip, mobility, low soreness
capacity: progressive lower-body strength and posterior-chain support
power: low-volume high-quality explosive work when appropriate
maintenance: lower volume during race or high-ride-load periods
technical_models.backend_use: Tie gym loading to rider level and ride calendar so strength improves tolerance without compromising key rides.

technical_models.name: Overtraining warning stack
technical_models.backend_use: A cluster of warning signs should pause progression even when planned training volume looks acceptable.

technical_models.name: Crash-risk gate
technical_models.backend_use: Regress route or skill demand before progressing speed, pack riding, descents, or technical terrain.

technical_models.name: Return-to-ride ladder
technical_models.backend_use: Progress only when same-day and next-day symptom response stays green.

tactical_rules.rule: If knee pain appears or rises during a ride, shift to easier gears, increase cadence within comfort, avoid standing climbs and hard accelerations, and shorten the session if symptoms continue.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Set next session to easy endurance or recovery, remove low-cadence torque work, and prompt saddle and cleat review.

tactical_rules.rule: If low-back discomfort builds with time in position, reduce aggressive aero or drop-bar exposure, add brief standing or posture breaks where safe, and cap duration before symptoms alter pedaling.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Progress duration conservatively and add trunk endurance, hip mobility, and fit review.

tactical_rules.rule: Hand numbness, tingling, loss of grip control, or weakness is a stop-pressure signal, not a cue to push through.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Shorten the ride if symptoms persist, prompt reach/bar/hood/glove/contact review, and avoid long continuous trainer sessions in one hand position.

tactical_rules.rule: Persistent perineal or genital numbness, urinary/genital symptoms, or saddle sores with skin breakdown require stopping the provoking exposure and seeking qualified review.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Do not progress ride duration; prompt saddle, short, chamois, hygiene, and bike-fit review with medical referral when symptoms persist.

tactical_rules.rule: For Achilles or calf symptoms, remove sprinting, hard starts, steep climbs, and big-gear low-cadence work before reducing all cycling.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Use easy flat spinning and review cleat, saddle height, recent load increase, and off-bike calf loading.

tactical_rules.rule: After a meaningful fit or equipment change, reduce total load and intensity for several rides and monitor knee, Achilles, back, hand, and saddle response.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Mark the change as a load spike risk and avoid long rides, races, or hard climbing immediately after the change.

tactical_rules.rule: Indoor trainer sessions should include planned posture and hand-position changes because fixed position, heat, and low coasting can raise contact-point and fatigue load.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Cap continuous indoor duration for beginners or symptomatic riders and include cooling, hydration, and position breaks.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not start higher-speed or traffic-exposed rides without helmet, working brakes, inflated tires, secure wheels, functioning drivetrain, and visibility appropriate to conditions.
tactical_rules.backend_action: If the pre-ride gate fails, replace with indoor trainer, skills practice in safe area, or maintenance task.

tactical_rules.rule: Beginners should not be assigned fast group rides, technical descents, or high-traffic routes until braking, cornering, shoulder checking, signaling, and straight-line control are reliable.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Prioritize traffic-free route selection and handling skill progressions before speed or pack exposure.

tactical_rules.rule: If pain is worse the next morning, do not progress the next ride even if the previous session was completed.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Repeat, reduce, or regress the prior dose and review fit or tissue-specific exposure.

tactical_rules.rule: Avoid stacking hard intervals, long rides, hill repeats, and heavy lower-body strength in the same short recovery window unless the rider is trained for that density.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Separate key bike sessions and heavy gym work, or reduce volume during build weeks.

tactical_rules.rule: When performance drops while RPE rises across repeated sessions, hold intensity progression and schedule recovery before adding more fitness work.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Reduce volume and intensity, assess sleep, fueling, stress, illness, and total sport load, then resume only when markers normalize.

tactical_rules.rule: After a crash with head impact, loss of consciousness, suspected fracture, persistent swelling, neurological symptoms, chest or abdominal pain, or inability to bear weight, do not assign return-to-ride until medical evaluation is complete.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Block training progression and provide emergency or medical referral messaging based on severity.

tactical_rules.rule: Avoid new saddles, shoes, cleats, aggressive bar positions, crank changes, or large fit changes close to an event.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Keep equipment stable and use race week only for known setups unless a safety issue forces change.

tactical_rules.rule: Wet roads, loose gravel, technical MTB trails, darkness, heavy traffic, or high wind should reduce speed, descending, cornering, and group-riding demands.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Offer safer route, indoor alternative, or lower-skill session when environmental risk is high.

physical_demands.description: Ability to tolerate thousands of flexion-extension cycles under changing torque, cadence, and climbing demands.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Progress low-cadence torque, hill repeats, and threshold work after symptom-free base riding and fit stability.

physical_demands.description: Sustained pelvic and spinal support while producing power from a flexed cycling posture.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Include anti-extension, anti-rotation, hip-hinge, and breathing-control work; progress aero or long rides gradually.

physical_demands.description: Hip flexion tolerance, hip extension strength, gluteal support, and single-leg control affect pelvic posture and knee tracking.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Pair mobility with strength; avoid only stretching a rider who lacks hip control under fatigue.

physical_demands.description: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal extensors, and calves support force production and posture during seated and standing efforts.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Use progressive hinges, split squats, bridges, calf work, and deadlift patterns where appropriate.

physical_demands.description: Upper-back, scapular, and neck endurance support head position and relaxed steering during long rides or aero positions.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Add scapular endurance, thoracic mobility, relaxed grip cues, and reach/bar review when symptoms appear.

physical_demands.description: Cyclists must tolerate handlebar pressure and vibration without sustained nerve compression or excessive wrist extension.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Program position changes, contact-point checks, grip relaxation, and symptom escalation rules.

physical_demands.description: Skin, soft tissue, and perineal structures must tolerate pressure, friction, heat, sweat, and duration.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Progress saddle time gradually and monitor numbness, sores, chafing, and hygiene practices.

physical_demands.description: Calf-Achilles complex handles repetitive ankle control, standing climbing, sprint starts, and shoe-pedal interface demands.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Use progressive calf strength and avoid abrupt jumps in sprinting, hill work, or cleat changes.

physical_demands.description: Aerobic fitness supports repeated endurance rides and recovery between harder sessions.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Beginners should build easy ride consistency before dense threshold, VO2, or sprint work.

physical_demands.description: Low-cadence climbing, big-gear intervals, starts, and headwind riding increase joint and tendon force demands.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Track torque exposure separately from total duration, especially in knee and Achilles symptom history.

physical_demands.description: MTB and gravel add grip, shoulder, trunk, and vibration tolerance beyond smooth-road metabolic load.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Do not equate road hours to off-road readiness; include handling skill and upper-body/trunk preparation.

physical_demands.description: Heat, dehydration, poor sleep, and life stress can make the same workout produce a much higher internal load.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Adjust sessions using RPE, heart rate drift, sleep, mood, and recovery markers, not only planned watts.

physical_demands.description: Safe braking, cornering, scanning, and decision-making must persist late in rides and after hard intervals.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Reduce technical descents, group riding, or traffic exposure when fatigue is high.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Anterior knee pain
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Reduce torque and intensity, review saddle and cleats, favor easy spinning, and reintroduce climbing gradually.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Lateral knee or ITB-region pain
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Hold long duration and hard climbs, review cleat float/rotation and stance width, and resume with short easy rides.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Low-back pain
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Reduce position exposure, cap duration, add trunk/hip work, and review reach/bar drop/saddle setup.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Neck and shoulder pain
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Reduce aggressive position time, add upper-back/scapular endurance, prompt fit review, and vary hand positions.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Hand, wrist, median, or ulnar nerve symptoms
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Stop persistent pressure, shorten rides, review cockpit fit, and refer if neurological signs persist.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Saddle and perineal numbness
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Do not progress duration; review saddle design/tilt/position, add pressure relief, and refer if symptoms persist.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Saddle sores and skin breakdown
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Reduce saddle time, improve hygiene/equipment, avoid riding on open lesions, and seek medical review for infection signs.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Achilles tendon pain
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Remove high-tendon-load exposures, use pain-monitoring, add progressive calf loading when appropriate, and review fit.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Calf cramping or strain risk
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Reduce sprint and climbing work, check recovery and hydration, review foot-pedal position, and rebuild calf strength.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Fit or equipment change spike
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Treat as new load, reduce training stress temporarily, and reverse or refine the change if symptoms persist.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Indoor trainer overuse
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Use fans, hydration, position breaks, shorter intervals of continuous sitting, and conservative progression.

injury_or_load_risks.name: High-intensity density overload
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Reduce intensity density, preserve easy rides, and progress hard sessions only after recovery markers normalize.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Long-ride duration spike
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Increase long ride gradually and monitor contact points, fueling, and next-day pain before adding intensity.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Preseason or block transition injury risk
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Use conservative ramps, record baseline tolerances, and avoid adding fit changes during the same window.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Nonfunctional overreaching or overtraining risk
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Stop progression, reduce load, assess recovery factors, and resume only when performance and wellness recover.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Crash or fall risk
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Regress environment and skill demand, require pre-ride checks, and block return after serious crash red flags.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Beginner contact-point overload
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Keep rides short and frequent, build comfort before intensity, and review setup early.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Aero-position intolerance
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Progress aero time gradually and separate position adaptation from hard intervals until tolerance is stable.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Under-triaged crash recovery
injury_or_load_risks.plan_response: Require medical assessment for red flags and mechanical inspection before outdoor riding resumes.

training_implications.name: Beginner comfort before intensity
training_implications.instruction: Build short, easy, repeatable rides that establish saddle, neck, hand, back, and knee tolerance before intervals, fast groups, or long climbs.
training_implications.backend_use: Beginner plans should include comfort checks after every ride and cap duration increases when contact-point symptoms appear.

training_implications.name: Knee symptoms reduce torque first
training_implications.instruction: When knee symptoms are mild and non-traumatic, remove big-gear torque, steep climbing, and hard accelerations before eliminating all easy spinning.
training_implications.backend_use: Preserve low-risk aerobic activity if symptoms remain green and next-day response is normal.

training_implications.name: Low-back plans pair fit and capacity
training_implications.instruction: Low-back mitigation should combine cockpit/posture review, hip mobility, trunk endurance, posterior-chain strength, and gradual duration exposure.
training_implications.backend_use: Avoid writing plans that prescribe only stretching or only bike-fit changes.

training_implications.name: Hand numbness is not normal adaptation
training_implications.instruction: Do not progress ride duration while neurological hand symptoms persist or worsen.
training_implications.backend_use: Trigger contact-point review and referral if numbness, weakness, or grip-control changes persist after rides.

training_implications.name: Saddle time progression
training_implications.instruction: Progress total saddle time and longest ride separately from power-zone progression because skin and perineal tissues may be the limiting factor.
training_implications.backend_use: For saddle symptoms, reduce duration and add setup/hygiene checks before adding intensity.

training_implications.name: Achilles exposure order
training_implications.instruction: Reintroduce Achilles-loading exposures in order: easy flat spin, longer flat spin, gentle rolling terrain, seated climbs, controlled standing climbs, then sprints or steep climbs.
training_implications.backend_use: Use next-day tendon response as the gate between steps.

training_implications.name: Minimum effective strength dose
training_implications.instruction: Use two weekly strength sessions in general preparation when possible, then reduce to maintenance during race-heavy or high-volume riding periods.
training_implications.backend_use: Avoid high-soreness gym work near key interval, race, or long-ride days.

training_implications.name: Strength exercise families
training_implications.instruction: Prioritize squat or split-squat patterns, hip hinges, step-ups, calf raises, trunk anti-motion work, scapular/upper-back endurance, and mobility matched to position demands.
training_implications.backend_use: Map exercise selection to injury history and rider level instead of random circuits.

training_implications.name: Track load spikes
training_implications.instruction: Record sudden changes in weekly hours, long-ride duration, climbing, sprint count, indoor trainer time, and fit setup as separate risk events.
training_implications.backend_use: Use load-change flags to adjust the next seven to fourteen days of training.

training_implications.name: Load response over plan completion
training_implications.instruction: Do not reward completing prescribed watts if the rider reports high pain, neurological symptoms, worsening fatigue, or poor next-day recovery.
training_implications.backend_use: Plan adherence should be interpreted alongside symptom and wellness response.

training_implications.name: Return-to-ride increases duration before intensity
training_implications.instruction: After injury, illness, crash, or long break, rebuild easy flat duration before adding hills, low cadence, tempo, threshold, VO2, sprints, or group rides.
training_implications.backend_use: Return ladders should progress one stressor at a time.

training_implications.name: Crash safety overrides fitness targets
training_implications.instruction: A planned high-value workout should be replaced when equipment, weather, light, traffic, or fatigue creates unacceptable crash risk.
training_implications.backend_use: Offer indoor, skills, recovery, or maintenance alternatives instead of forcing outdoor completion.

training_implications.name: Aero adaptation blocks
training_implications.instruction: Time-trial and triathlon positions need progressive exposure blocks because neck, shoulder, low-back, hip, saddle, and handling tolerance may lag aerobic fitness.
training_implications.backend_use: Separate position-tolerance sessions from maximal interval goals during early adaptation.

training_implications.name: Multi-sport total load
training_implications.instruction: For triathletes or multi-sport users, cycling load decisions must consider run, gym, swim, work, sleep, and illness stress.
training_implications.backend_use: Do not increase cycling simply because cycling symptoms are low if total athlete load is high.

training_implications.name: Group rides are intensity and safety load
training_implications.instruction: Fast group rides should count as high-intensity, decision-making, handling, and crash-risk exposure, not only endurance mileage.
training_implications.backend_use: Avoid placing hard intervals immediately before or after uncontrolled group rides for non-advanced riders.

training_implications.name: New-bike onboarding
training_implications.instruction: A new bike should begin with short comfort rides, gradual position exposure, and symptom logging before long rides or racing.
training_implications.backend_use: Create a new-equipment adaptation microcycle when the user reports a new bike or major component change.

training_implications.name: Fatigue changes bike handling
training_implications.instruction: When fatigue is high, reduce technical descents, traffic exposure, wet-road cornering, and fast pack-riding even if the planned metabolic work is easy.
training_implications.backend_use: Readiness adjustments should include safety exposure, not only training-zone changes.

training_implications.name: Medical referral red flags
training_implications.instruction: Escalate sharp traumatic pain, suspected fracture, head injury signs, neurological symptoms, persistent saddle numbness, infection signs, chest symptoms, and unexplained severe fatigue.
training_implications.backend_use: The backend should provide referral messaging and avoid substituting training modifications for medical evaluation.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling knee pain: reduce torque and review fit
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Knee pain during or after cycling, especially with climbing, low cadence, or recent fit changes.
backend_records_to_create.action: Reduce big-gear torque, hard starts, steep climbs, and interval density; prompt saddle height, saddle setback, cleat, cadence, and recent-load review.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling low back: position plus capacity
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Low-back symptoms linked to duration, aero posture, drops, or fatigue.
backend_records_to_create.action: Cap position exposure, review reach/bar drop/saddle setup, and add trunk endurance, hip mobility, and posterior-chain strength.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling hand numbness: contact-point review
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Hand numbness, tingling, weakness, or grip-control changes during or after riding.
backend_records_to_create.action: Stop sustained pressure, shorten rides, vary hand position, review reach/bar/hood/glove setup, and refer if neurological signs persist.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling saddle numbness: red flag
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Persistent perineal or genital numbness, urinary/genital symptoms, or worsening saddle sores.
backend_records_to_create.action: Stop progressing duration, prompt saddle/shorts/chamois/fit review, and seek qualified medical or fit assessment for persistent symptoms.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling Achilles: deload high tendon exposures
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Achilles or calf pain, morning stiffness, or symptoms after climbing/sprints.
backend_records_to_create.action: Remove sprints, steep climbs, hard starts, and big-gear work; use easy flat spinning and next-day pain gates.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling fit change counts as load change
backend_records_to_create.trigger: New bike, saddle, shoes, cleats, cockpit, crank, or aero setup.
backend_records_to_create.action: Schedule short easy adaptation rides, avoid major intensity or volume spikes, and monitor new symptoms for two weeks.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling strength: general preparation
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Base or general preparation phase with adequate recovery.
backend_records_to_create.action: Use progressive lower-body strength, posterior-chain work, trunk anti-motion, calf capacity, scapular endurance, and mobility; avoid excessive soreness.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling strength: maintenance during high ride load
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Race phase, high-volume block, or frequent hard rides.
backend_records_to_create.action: Reduce gym volume while preserving strength stimulus; place heavy work away from key intervals and long rides.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling pain monitoring: next-day gate
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Any overuse symptom during a return-to-ride or build block.
backend_records_to_create.action: Progress only if symptoms remain mild, do not increase during the ride, and return to baseline by the next morning.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling overtraining warning hold
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Performance drops while RPE, fatigue, poor sleep, mood disturbance, illness, or soreness persists.
backend_records_to_create.action: Hold progression, reduce load, check recovery and life-stress factors, and resume only after markers improve.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling weekly load channels
backend_records_to_create.action: Use these fields to detect non-obvious spikes and tissue-specific risks.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling pre-ride equipment gate
backend_records_to_create.action: Require helmet, brake check, tire pressure/condition, secure wheels, drivetrain check, lights/visibility when needed, and route risk review.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling crash return: medical and mechanical screen
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Crash, fall, head impact, suspected fracture, neurological symptoms, or damaged bike.
backend_records_to_create.action: Block normal training until medical red flags and bike mechanical safety are addressed.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling beginner comfort foundation
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Beginner, returning rider, or rider with low saddle/handling tolerance.
backend_records_to_create.action: Use short easy rides, traffic-safe routes, basic handling, fit checks, and comfort monitoring before high-intensity or long endurance work.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling return-to-ride ladder
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Return after injury, illness, crash, or long layoff.
backend_records_to_create.action: Progress from short easy flat rides to duration, gentle terrain, tempo, climbing, sprinting, group riding, and event-specific work one step at a time.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling indoor trainer contact management
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Indoor trainer sessions longer than short recovery duration or rider with hand/saddle/back symptoms.
backend_records_to_create.action: Add cooling, hydration, posture breaks, hand-position variation, and conservative continuous-sitting progression.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling group ride counts as hard day
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Fast, hilly, technical, or competitive group ride planned.
backend_records_to_create.action: Count as intensity plus handling and crash-risk exposure; avoid stacking with dense intervals or heavy lower-body gym work unless advanced and recovered.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling aero-position adaptation
backend_records_to_create.trigger: Time trial, triathlon, or aero-bar position introduced.
backend_records_to_create.action: Build aero time gradually, monitor neck/back/saddle symptoms, and avoid maximal sessions until position tolerance is stable.
